subtasks.title: Implement backup service core
subtasks.description: Create BackupService class with methods to: discover backup targets (volumes, configs, databases), calculate backup size, create compressed archives (tar.gz), and generate backup manifests with checksums.
subtasks.notes:
Implemented comprehensive BackupService class with the following functionality:
- discoverBackupTargets(): Discovers configs, databases, metadata, and volumes from running containers
- calculateBackupSize(): Calculates total backup size with support for volumes and container paths
- createBackupArchive(): Creates compressed tar.gz archives with progress tracking
- generateManifest(): Generates backup manifests with SHA256 checksums
- validateBackup(): Validates backup integrity using checksums
- Helper functions: archiveVolume(), archiveContainerPath(), getDockerVolumes(), getRunningContainers(), etc.

Supports all major media stack services: *Arr apps (Sonarr, Radarr, Prowlarr, etc.), media servers (Plex, Jellyfin), download clients (qBittorrent, Deluge, etc.), and request management (Overseerr, Jellyseerr).

subtasks.title: Implement encryption module
subtasks.description: Create encryption utilities using Node.js crypto for AES-256-GCM encryption of backup archives. Support password-based key derivation (PBKDF2).
subtasks.notes:
Implemented comprehensive encryption utilities module with AES-256-GCM encryption and PBKDF2 key derivation:

**Core Functions:**
- encryptFile(): Stream-based encryption for large backup archives
- decryptFile(): Stream-based decryption with authentication verification
- verifyPassword(): Quick password validation without full decryption
- getEncryptionInfo(): Returns encryption algorithm details

**Security Features:**
- AES-256-GCM authenticated encryption (256-bit keys)
- PBKDF2 key derivation (100,000 iterations, SHA256)
- Random salt (256-bit) and IV (128-bit) per file
- Authentication tag prevents tampering
- Custom file format with magic bytes (MSBKUP01) and version header

**Implementation Details:**
- Streaming encryption/decryption for memory efficiency
- Embedded metadata in file header (salt, IV, auth tag)
- Automatic cleanup of partial files on errors
- Detailed error handling with password verification
- Follows existing patterns: createLogger(), getErrorMessage(), async/await

The module provides production-ready encryption for backup archives with strong security guarantees.

subtasks.title: Implement storage destination adapters
subtasks.description: Create adapter pattern for backup destinations: LocalAdapter (filesystem), S3Adapter (AWS SDK), RcloneAdapter (shell wrapper). Each adapter handles upload, download, list, and delete operations.
subtasks.notes:
Implemented comprehensive adapter pattern for backup destinations with the following components:

**Base Adapter Interface (destinationAdapter.ts):**
- DestinationAdapter interface with upload, download, list, delete, and testConnection methods
- BackupFileInfo interface for file metadata
- TransferProgress interface for progress tracking
- Factory function createAdapter() that dynamically loads the appropriate adapter based on destination type

**LocalAdapter (localAdapter.ts):**
- File operations using fs/promises for async filesystem access
- Upload/download via copyFile for efficient local transfers
- List operation with filtering for .tar.gz and .enc backup files
- Delete operation using unlink
- Connection test creates a temporary file to verify write access
- Progress callbacks for transfer tracking
- Proper error handling and cleanup

**S3Adapter (s3Adapter.ts):**
- Dynamic import of @aws-sdk/client-s3 (lazy loading)
- Support for S3-compatible services (AWS S3, MinIO, etc.)
- Stream-based upload/download with progress tracking
- forcePathStyle for compatibility with non-AWS S3 services
- Uses PutObjectCommand, GetObjectCommand, ListObjectsV2Command, DeleteObjectCommand, HeadBucketCommand
- Proper error handling with cleanup of partial files
- Path prefix support for organized backups

**RcloneAdapter (rcloneAdapter.ts):**
- Shell wrapper around rclone CLI using runCommand()
- Support for all rclone-compatible remotes (Google Drive, Dropbox, etc.)
- Upload/download using 'rclone copyto' with stats tracking
- List operation using 'rclone lsl' (with 'ls' fallback)
- Delete operation using 'rclone delete'
- Connection test using 'rclone lsd'
- Generous timeouts (1 hour) for large file transfers
- Parses rclone output for file metadata

**Code Quality:**
- Follows existing patterns: createLogger(), getErrorMessage(), runCommand()
- All imports use .js extensions (ES modules)
- TypeScript types match backup.ts interfaces
- Comprehensive JSDoc comments
- Proper error handling with detailed logging
- Progress callback support for all adapters
- Cleanup of partial files on errors

subtasks.title: Create backup API routes
subtasks.description: Implement Fastify routes: POST /api/backup/create (start backup), GET /api/backup/status/:id (progress), GET /api/backup/list (list backups), POST /api/backup/validate (verify integrity), DELETE /api/backup/:id (remove backup).
subtasks.notes:
Implemented comprehensive backup API routes for control-server:

**Routes Implemented:**
1. POST /api/backup/create - Start a new backup operation
   - Validates backup config with Zod schema
   - Returns backup ID and starts async backup process
   - Tracks progress in memory for status queries

2. GET /api/backup/status/:id - Get progress of active backup
   - Returns real-time progress including status, current operation, items/bytes processed, transfer speed, ETA
   - Supports all backup statuses: initializing, discovering, archiving, encrypting, uploading, completed, failed

3. POST /api/backup/list - List available backups from destination
   - Downloads and parses manifest files from destination
   - Supports pagination with limit/offset
   - Returns backup history with metadata
   - Tests connection before listing

4. POST /api/backup/validate - Validate backup integrity
   - Downloads manifest and archive files
   - Verifies checksums using validateBackupIntegrity
   - Supports encrypted backups with decryption password
   - Returns validation results with detailed errors

5. DELETE /api/backup/:id - Delete backup from destination
   - Downloads manifest to find all associated files
   - Deletes all archive files and manifest
   - Handles both encrypted and unencrypted files
   - Returns list of deleted files and any errors

6. GET /api/backup/discover - Discover available backup targets (bonus)
   - Discovers all backup targets from running containers
   - Calculates total backup size
   - Returns list of targets with metadata

**Implementation Details:**
- Follows existing patterns from docker.ts and arr.ts routes
- Uses Zod schemas for request validation
- Proper error handling with getErrorMessage()
- Uses createLogger() for logging
- Async/await throughout
- In-memory progress tracking for active backups
- Integrates with BackupService, destination adapters, and encryption utilities
- All imports use .js extensions (ES modules)
- TypeScript types properly applied
- Status codes: 200 (success), 202 (accepted), 400 (bad request), 404 (not found), 500 (error), 503 (unavailable)

**executeBackup() Helper:**
- Runs backup operation asynchronously
- Updates progress at each stage
- Handles discovery, archiving, encryption, and upload
- Proper cleanup of temporary files
- Comprehensive error handling

The routes provide a complete API for backup operations and integrate seamlessly with the existing backup service infrastructure.

subtasks.title: Implement backup scheduler
subtasks.description: Create scheduler using node-cron for automated backups. Support configurable intervals (daily/weekly/monthly), retention policies (keep N backups), and health check notifications.
subtasks.notes:
Implemented comprehensive backup scheduler service using node-cron:

**Core Features:**
- Schedule management with persistent storage (JSON file in data/schedules/)
- Cron job scheduling with daily/weekly/monthly frequencies
- Automatic backup execution on schedule
- Retention policy enforcement (keep N backups, auto-delete old ones)
- Health check tracking with consecutive failure monitoring

**Scheduler Functions:**
- initializeScheduler(): Load schedules from disk and start cron jobs
- shutdownScheduler(): Stop all active cron jobs gracefully
- addSchedule(): Create new backup schedule
- updateSchedule(): Update existing schedule (restarts cron job)
- deleteSchedule(): Remove schedule and stop cron job
- getSchedules(): List all schedules
- getSchedule(): Get specific schedule by ID
- getScheduleHealth(): Get health status for all schedules
- triggerSchedule(): Manually trigger a scheduled backup

**Scheduled Backup Execution:**
- executeScheduledBackup(): Runs complete backup workflow
  - Discovers backup targets if items are empty
  - Creates compressed archive
  - Encrypts if configured
  - Uploads to destination
  - Updates schedule metadata (lastRun, nextRun)
  - Tracks health status (lastAttempt, lastSuccess, lastError, consecutiveFailures)
  - Applies retention policy after successful backup
  - Cleans up temporary files

**Retention Policy:**
- applyRetentionPolicy(): Enforces retention count
  - Lists all backups from destination
  - Parses manifests to get creation dates
  - Sorts by date (newest first)
  - Deletes backups beyond retention count
  - Handles both encrypted and unencrypted backups
  - Cleans up all associated files (manifests + archives)

**Health Monitoring:**
- Tracks last attempt, last success, last error for each schedule
- Counts consecutive failures
- Logs warnings when failures exceed threshold (3+)
- Ready for future notification integration

**Cron Expression Conversion:**
- Daily: `MM HH * * *` (every day at specified time)
- Weekly: `MM HH * * 0` (every Sunday at specified time)
- Monthly: `MM HH 1 * *` (1st of month at specified time)
- Timezone: UTC

**Dependencies Added:**
- node-cron: ^3.0.3 (cron job scheduling)
- @types/node-cron: ^3.0.11 (TypeScript types)

**Implementation Details:**
- Follows existing patterns from metricsService.ts for persistence
- Uses createLogger() for structured logging
- Uses getErrorMessage() for error handling
- All imports use .js extensions (ES modules)
- In-memory Map for active cron jobs
- Persistent JSON storage for schedules
- Automatic directory creation for data/schedules
- Proper cleanup of temporary files after operations

The scheduler is production-ready with proper error handling, logging, and graceful shutdown support.

subtasks.title: Create backup API hooks
subtasks.description: Create React hooks for backup operations: useBackupCreate, useBackupProgress (polling), useBackupList, useRestoreExecute, useRestoreProgress. Handle loading, error, and success states.
subtasks.notes:
Created comprehensive React hooks for backup and restore operations in docs-site/src/hooks/useBackup.ts:

**Hooks Implemented:**

1. **useBackupDiscover()** - Discover available backup targets
   - Returns: targets array, totalSize, count
   - States: loading, error, data
   - Method: discover()

2. **useBackupCreate()** - Create a new backup
   - Accepts: BackupConfig (destination, items, encryption, name, schedule)
   - Returns: backupId
   - States: loading, error, data
   - Method: createBackup(config)

3. **useBackupProgress()** - Poll backup progress with automatic stop
   - Returns: BackupProgress object
   - States: loading, error, progress, isPolling
   - Methods: startPolling(backupId, interval), stopPolling()
   - Auto-stops when status is 'completed' or 'failed'
   - Default polling interval: 1000ms

4. **useBackupList()** - List available backups from destination
   - Accepts: BackupListOptions (destination, limit, offset)
   - Returns: backups array, total, limit, offset
   - States: loading, error, data
   - Method: listBackups(options)

5. **useRestorePreview()** - Preview backup contents before restoring
   - Accepts: RestorePreviewOptions (backupId, destination, decryptionPassword)
   - Returns: BackupPreview with items array and metadata
   - States: loading, error, data
   - Method: previewBackup(options)

6. **useRestoreExecute()** - Execute a restore operation
   - Accepts: RestoreConfig (backupId, destination, items, decryptionPassword, stopServices, createPreRestoreBackup)
   - Returns: restoreId
   - States: loading, error, data
   - Method: executeRestore(config)

7. **useRestoreProgress()** - Poll restore progress with automatic stop
   - Returns: RestoreProgress object
   - States: loading, error, progress, isPolling
   - Methods: startPolling(restoreId, interval), stopPolling()
   - Auto-stops when status is 'completed' or 'failed'
   - Default polling interval: 1000ms

**Implementation Details:**
- Follows existing patterns from useControlServerStatus.ts and useStreamingChat.ts
- Uses buildControlServerUrl() and controlServerAuthHeaders() from utils/controlServer
- Uses getErrorMessage() from utils/logging for consistent error handling
- All hooks use useState and useCallback for optimal performance
- Progress hooks use useRef and useEffect for polling intervals
- Proper cleanup of intervals on unmount
- TypeScript interfaces match backend API and backupStore types
- Comprehensive error handling with HTTP status checking
- Loading, error, and data states for all operations
- POST requests use Content-Type: application/json header

**API Endpoints Used:**
- GET /api/backup/discover
- POST /api/backup/create
- GET /api/backup/status/:id
- POST /api/backup/list
- POST /api/restore/preview
- POST /api/restore/execute
- GET /api/restore/status/:id

The hooks provide a complete React interface for all backup and restore operations with proper state management, error handling, and loading states.

subtasks.title: Create ReviewStep component
subtasks.description: Step 5: Review and execute. Summary of all settings. Start backup button. Progress display with: current step, percentage, estimated time remaining, transfer speed.
subtasks.notes:
Created comprehensive ReviewStep component for backup wizard with the following features:

**Component Structure:**
- Two-phase UI: Configuration Summary (before backup) and Progress Display (during backup)
- AnimatePresence for smooth transitions between phases
- Real-time progress updates via useBackupProgress hook with 1-second polling interval

**Configuration Summary (Pre-Backup):**
- Destination Summary: Shows configured destination with icon, type, and details
- Selected Items Summary: Lists all selected backup items with sizes, scrollable list
- Encryption Summary: Displays encryption status (enabled/disabled) with AES-256-GCM note
- Schedule Summary: Shows schedule configuration or "One-time manual backup"
- Backup Name: Displays optional backup name if provided
- Start Backup button with loading state

**Progress Display (During Backup):**
- Overall progress bar with percentage and bytes processed/total
- Status badge with appropriate icon (spinner/checkmark/error) and colored styling
- Current operation card showing what's happening now and which item is being processed
- Progress stats grid with three cards:
  - Items Processed: X/Y items counter with Database icon
  - Transfer Speed: MB/s or KB/s display with TrendingUp icon
  - Estimated Time: Formatted ETA with Timer icon
- Success banner when backup completes (green with checkmark)
- Error banner when backup fails (red with error message)

**Utility Functions:**
- formatBytes(): Converts bytes to human-readable sizes (B, KB, MB, GB, TB)
- formatSpeed(): Formats transfer speed as bytes/second
- formatETA(): Calculates and formats time remaining (hours, minutes, seconds)
- getDestinationName(): Returns friendly display name for destination

subtasks.title: Add backend unit tests
subtasks.description: Create vitest tests for backup service, encryption utilities, and destination adapters. Mock Docker commands and filesystem operations.
subtasks.notes:
Created comprehensive vitest tests for backup service, encryption utilities, and destination adapters with 817 lines of test code:

**Test Coverage:**

1. **Backup Service Tests (discoverBackupTargets, calculateBackupSize, validateBackup, container operations, restore operations):**
   - discoverBackupTargets(): Tests discovery from running containers with proper mocking of Docker commands
   - calculateBackupSize(): Tests size calculation from estimated sizes and volumes
   - validateBackup(): Tests checksum validation with matching and mismatching checksums
   - stopContainer() / startContainer(): Tests container lifecycle operations
   - extractBackupArchive(): Tests tar.gz extraction
   - restoreToVolume(): Tests Docker volume restoration
   - restoreToContainerPath(): Tests container path restoration

2. **Encryption Utilities Tests (encryptFile, decryptFile, verifyPassword):**
   - encryptFile(): Tests AES-256-GCM encryption with PBKDF2 key derivation, auth tag updates, cleanup on failure
   - decryptFile(): Tests decryption with correct password, invalid password detection, invalid file format handling
   - verifyPassword(): Tests password verification without full decryption
   - getEncryptionInfo(): Tests encryption algorithm details retrieval

3. **Local Adapter Tests (upload, download, list, delete, testConnection):**
   - upload(): Tests file copying to local destination with progress callbacks
   - download(): Tests file copying from local destination with progress callbacks
   - list(): Tests listing .tar.gz and .enc files, filtering, sorting by date
   - delete(): Tests file deletion from local destination
   - testConnection(): Tests path accessibility with test file creation

**Mocking Strategy:**
- Mocked Docker commands (runCommand) for all container and volume operations
- Mocked filesystem operations (fs/promises) for file I/O
- Mocked crypto functions for encryption/decryption testing
- Mocked streams (Readable, Writable) for file processing
- All mocks follow existing test patterns from bootstrap.test.ts and remote.test.ts

**Error Handling:**
- Tests verify proper error messages and cleanup on failures
- Tests confirm partial file cleanup on encryption/decryption errors
- Tests validate error propagation for Docker command failures

**Files Created:**
- control-server/test/backup.test.ts (817 lines)

The tests provide comprehensive coverage of the backup system's core functionality with proper mocking of external dependencies (Docker, filesystem, crypto). All tests follow vitest patterns established in the codebase.

subtasks.title: Add frontend smoke tests
subtasks.description: Create Playwright tests for backup wizard flow: destination setup, item selection, encryption config, schedule config, backup execution.
subtasks.notes:
Created comprehensive Playwright test suite for backup wizard flow in docs-site/tests/backup.spec.ts with 444 lines of test code:

**Test Coverage:**

1. **Full Wizard Flow Test:**
   - Navigates through all 5 steps (Destination → Selection → Encryption → Schedule → Review)
   - Tests local destination configuration with path input
   - Tests backup discovery and item selection (Select All functionality)
   - Tests encryption configuration with password and confirmation
   - Tests schedule configuration with daily frequency, time, and retention settings
   - Tests backup execution and progress tracking
   - Verifies completion status display

2. **Field Validation Tests:**
   - Validates required destination configuration
   - Validates at least one item must be selected
   - Validates encryption password required when encryption enabled
   - Verifies error toasts appear for validation failures

3. **S3 Destination Configuration Test:**
   - Tests S3 tab selection
   - Fills endpoint, bucket, access key, and secret key
   - Verifies form values persist

4. **Rclone Destination Configuration Test:**
   - Tests Rclone tab selection
   - Fills remote name and remote path
   - Verifies form values persist

5. **Optional Steps Test:**
   - Verifies encryption step can be skipped (toggle not enabled)
   - Verifies schedule step can be skipped (toggle not enabled)
   - Confirms wizard reaches review step without these optional configs

6. **Back Navigation Test:**
   - Tests navigation backwards through wizard steps
   - Verifies form state is preserved when going back
   - Checks destination path persists
   - Checks item selections persist

7. **Password Strength Indicator Test:**
   - Tests weak password shows appropriate strength level
   - Tests strong password shows better strength level
   - Verifies strength indicator updates in real-time

**Mocking Strategy:**
- Mocked all control-server API endpoints:
  - GET /api/backup/discover - Returns sample backup targets (config, database, volume)
  - POST /api/backup/test-connection - Returns successful connection
  - POST /api/backup/create - Returns backup ID
  - GET /api/backup/status/:id - Returns completed status with progress
- localStorage cleared before each test for fresh wizard state
- Follows existing Playwright patterns from smoke.spec.ts and settings.cockpit.spec.ts

**Implementation Details:**
- Uses Playwright's page.route() for API mocking
- Proper timeout handling (120s for full flow test)
- Accessibility-focused selectors (getByRole, getByText)
- Fallback logic for optional UI elements
- Console logging for test progress tracking
- Error handling with .catch(() => false) for optional elements

**Files Created:**
- docs-site/tests/backup.spec.ts (444 lines)

The test suite provides comprehensive coverage of the backup wizard user journey with proper validation testing and state management verification. Tests follow all project patterns and conventions established in existing Playwright tests.
